project.name: NeuroMorphicToolKit
project.description: A unified neuromorphic computing toolkit (NMTK) that bridges neuroscience, software engineering, and hardware robotics into a single cohesive platform for spiking neural network R&D workflows.

nodes.summary: Shell script that auto-detects project type (Poetry, pip, Flutter) and runs CDD-PBT validation via pytest or flutter test for a given module directory.
nodes.name: cdd_validation.sh

nodes.summary: CLI tool that generates GitHub issues for each NMTK module requesting CDD-PBT migration, using the gh CLI with a templated issue body and optional dry-run mode.
nodes.name: generate_cdd_pbt_issues.py
main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI args and iterates over NMTK modules to create GitHub issues via gh CLI or print dry-run output.

Pydantic contract models for Neuro-Dream-Hand hardware integration covering HITL serial bridge, sensor frames, EMG streams, latency requirements, fault injection, crossbar export, and drop-test validation based on SPEC.md phases 4-5.
nodes.name: hardware_contracts.py
SerialBridgeContract
nodes.summary: Contract for Teensy serial bridge protocol enforcing grip range [0,1], supported baud rates, and Nengo dt=0.002 matching.

nodes.name: EMGStreamContract
nodes.summary: Contract for OpenBCI Ganglion EMG data stream enforcing 1-4 channels, Nyquist-limited bandpass, and encoding neuron count.

nodes.name: HITLLatencyContract
nodes.summary: Contract enforcing HITL latency requirements: median roundtrip under 4ms and p95 under 2ms for Teensy USB serial.

nodes.name: FaultInjectionContract
nodes.summary: Contract limiting fault injection fractions (dead neurons, stuck-at, weight noise) to 30% max per SPEC 5.1.

nodes.name: CrossbarExportContract
nodes.summary: Contract for crossbar weight-to-conductance mapping enforcing g_min < g_max > 0 for physical conductance export.

nodes.name: DropTestContract
nodes.summary: Contract for drop-test sim-to-real gap validation, rejecting gaps exceeding 15 percentage points.

Hypothesis property-based tests for Neuro-Dream-Hand hardware contracts covering serial protocol grip ranges, sensor ADC bounds, EMG encoding outputs, fault injection limits, crossbar conductance, and drop-test gap acceptance.
nodes.name: test_hitl_properties.py
TestSerialProtocolProperties
nodes.summary: Property-based test class verifying grip value acceptance/rejection and uint16 roundtrip precision for SerialBridgeContract.

nodes.name: TestFaultInjectionProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying fault injection fractions within [0, 0.30] are accepted and fractions > 30% are rejected.

nodes.name: TestDropTestProperties
nodes.summary: Property test verifying sim-to-real gap acceptance when within 15 percentage points and rejection otherwise.

Pydantic contract models for NeuroBench benchmarking covering benchmark definitions, results, regression detection with delta-percentage thresholds, robustness curves with fault sweeps, and cross-target hardware comparisons.
nodes.name: benchmark_contracts.py
BenchmarkDefinitionContract
nodes.summary: Contract defining benchmark metadata with typed task types (grip_stability, spike_classification, etc.) and scoring metric.

nodes.name: RegressionCheckContract
nodes.summary: Contract for regression detection comparing baseline vs current values with configurable percentage threshold and direction awareness.

nodes.name: RobustnessCurveContract
nodes.summary: Contract for fault sweep robustness curves enforcing consistent array lengths and minimum 5 seeds for confidence intervals.

nodes.name: CrossTargetComparisonContract
nodes.summary: Contract for cross-target hardware comparison with unit-range validation on accuracy and spike fidelity metrics.

Pydantic contract models for NeuroChip hardware deployment covering target profiles (Teensy, Loihi, Akida, SpiNNaker, BrainScaleS), weight quantization, fault sweeps, power/latency estimation, and Teensy firmware artifact validation.
nodes.name: deployment_contracts.py
HardwareTargetContract
nodes.summary: Contract for hardware target profiles specifying neuron capacity, supported models, bit widths, memory, and IO for five neuromorphic platforms.

nodes.name: QuantizationContract
nodes.summary: Contract for weight quantization enforcing supported bit widths {2,4,6,8,16,32}, accuracy in [0,1], and positive memory reduction factor.

nodes.name: LatencyEstimateContract
nodes.summary: Contract for latency estimation enforcing best <= typical <= worst ordering and positive latency values.

nodes.name: TeensyFirmwareContract
nodes.summary: Contract validating Teensy firmware package completeness: .ino file, network_params.h, lif_engine.h, and README must all be present.
Hypothesis property-based tests for NeuroChip deployment contracts covering quantization bit width acceptance/rejection, latency ordering invariants, and fault sweep rate bounds.
nodes.name: test_deployment_properties.py
TestQuantizationProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying supported and unsupported bit widths, plus a metamorphic test that higher bit-width should preserve more accuracy.

nodes.name: TestLatencyProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying latency ordering invariant (best <= typical <= worst) acceptance and inverted ordering rejection.
Package init re-exporting all NeuroCNL contracts (neuron params, hardware export, pipeline) through a consolidated __all__ list of 15 contract classes.
nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.summary: Pydantic contract models for neuromorphic hardware export targets (Loihi 2, SpiNNaker, Teensy 4.1) with platform-specific constraints on weights, neuron counts, memory, delays, and C header completeness validation.
nodes.name: hardware_export.py
LoihiExportContract
nodes.summary: Contract for Intel Loihi 2 export enforcing 8-bit weight quantization range, 1024 neurons per neurocore, and 0-62 timestep delay limits.

nodes.name: SpiNNakerExportContract
nodes.summary: Contract for SpiNNaker export enforcing s16.15 fixed-point weight range and 255 neurons per core limit.

nodes.name: TeensyExportContract
nodes.summary: Contract for Teensy 4.1 export enforcing 1MB RAM memory budget with neuron/connection size estimation and valid bit widths.

nodes.name: CHeaderContract
nodes.summary: Contract validating generated C header completeness: include guard, neuron params, weight array, and topology array sections.

Pydantic contract models for NeuroCNL neuron parameters encoding physics-based invariants for LIF neurons, synaptic connections (with inhibitory sign enforcement and biological delay bounds), STDP learning rules, and population/ensemble configurations.
nodes.name: neuron_params.py
LIFNeuronContract
nodes.summary: Contract for Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neuron enforcing positive refractory/tau, threshold above resting potential, reset below threshold, and correct membrane decay direction.

nodes.name: SynapticContract
nodes.summary: Contract for synaptic connections enforcing negative weights for inhibitory synapses and biological axonal delay range (max 150ms).

nodes.name: STDPContract
nodes.summary: Contract for STDP learning rules enforcing positive learning rate, biologically plausible window (0-100ms), valid rule types (PES/BCM/OJA/STDP), and weight_min < weight_max.

nodes.name: PopulationContract
nodes.summary: Contract for neuron population/ensemble parameters enforcing positive neuron count, dimensions, and radius.

nodes.name: pipeline_contracts.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic v2 contracts enforcing shape and validity of data flowing through the neurocnl pipeline stages: parse, validate, generate, simulate, and assert. Includes API response contracts for REST endpoints.

nodes.name: CNLParseResultContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model validating a single parsed CNL sentence, enforcing concept membership against a fixed set of 13 neuromorphic concepts like threshold_firing and stdp_learning.

nodes.name: SimulationResultContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for simulation output enforcing positive duration and timestep dt within (0, 0.1] range, plus wall-time tracking.

nodes.name: SimulationSummaryContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for simulation summary statistics enforcing non-negative spike counts and firing rates for sensory and motor populations.

nodes.name: AssertionResultContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for Layer 3 assertion execution results, tracking passed/failed counts and return code with non-negative count validation.

nodes.name: ParseAPIResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic model defining the POST /api/parse REST response shape with results list and valid/error counts.

nodes.name: SimulateAPIResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic model defining the POST /api/simulate REST response shape including duration, dt, wall_time, motor_output, optional probes and summary.

nodes.name: test_physics_properties.py
nodes.summary: Hypothesis property-based tests verifying universal physics laws for neurocnl contracts: LIF neuron invariants, contract rejection, synaptic constraints, Loihi hardware limits, and metamorphic relationships between parameters.

nodes.name: TestPhysicsInvariants
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying that for ALL valid LIF neuron parameters: threshold exceeds resting potential, reset never exceeds threshold, membrane decay direction is correct, and refractory period limits max firing rate below 1 MHz.

nodes.name: TestContractRejection
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying that LIFNeuronContract always rejects invalid parameters: threshold at or below resting potential, zero or negative tau, and zero or negative refractory period.

nodes.name: TestSynapticProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests for synaptic connection contracts verifying that positive weights with inhibitory flag and negative axonal delays are always rejected.

nodes.name: TestLoihiProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests for Loihi hardware export contracts verifying weight and neuron count acceptance limits, rejection of out-of-range values, and quantization roundtrip precision within 1 LSB.

nodes.name: TestMetamorphicProperties
nodes.summary: Metamorphic property tests verifying relational invariants: larger tau implies slower membrane decay rate, and longer refractory period implies lower maximum firing rate.

nodes.name: TestCNLPipelineProperties
nodes.summary: End-to-end pipeline property tests requiring neurocnl installation, verifying that valid CNL specs always pass L1+L2 validation and negative thresholds fail or parse differently.

nodes.name: orchestration_contracts.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic v2 domain contracts for NeuroHub suite orchestration covering port assignments, health checks, cross-app projects, workflow steps/templates, member roles, and activity feed entries.

nodes.name: SuitePortContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model defining default port assignments for all six neuromorphic suite services (8000-8005) with a model validator ensuring no port conflicts.

nodes.name: WorkflowStepContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for pipeline workflow steps with HTTP method, failure handling strategy (halt/warn/skip), and timeout validation between 1 and 3600 seconds.

nodes.name: WorkflowTemplateContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for workflow templates requiring at least one WorkflowStepContract, with built-in flag for system-provided templates.

nodes.name: ProjectContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for cross-app projects linking neurosim, neurochip, neurobench, and neurosense resources with non-empty name validation.

nodes.name: signal_contracts.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic v2 domain contracts for NeuroSense biosignal processing covering device discovery, signal quality metrics, spike encoding configuration, application presets, latency requirements, and recording sessions.

nodes.name: DeviceContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for biosignal device discovery enforcing device type literals (OpenBCI, Muse, BITalino, generic_serial), channel count 1-8, and sample rate.

nodes.name: EncodingConfigContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for spike encoding configuration supporting rate, temporal, and delta methods with positive rate and phase bin validators.

nodes.name: ApplicationPresetContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for application presets defining filter bandpass, notch frequency, encoding method, and channel mapping with model validator ensuring low < high bandpass.

nodes.name: DisplayLatencyContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model enforcing the 50ms maximum acquisition-to-display latency requirement from NSe-SA1 specification.

nodes.name: PipelineLatencyContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model enforcing the 100ms maximum end-to-end pipeline latency requirement from NSe-PI1 specification.

nodes.name: test_encoding_properties.py
nodes.summary: Hypothesis property-based tests for NeuroSense signal processing contracts covering encoding method validity, device channel limits, latency bounds, bandpass filter validation, and signal quality classification.

nodes.name: TestEncodingProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying all three encoding methods (rate, temporal, delta) are accepted and zero or negative rate_max_hz is always rejected.

nodes.name: TestDeviceProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying device channel count acceptance for 1-8 channels and rejection for counts exceeding the NSe-SA1 8-channel limit.

nodes.name: TestLatencyProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying display latency acceptance under 50ms, rejection over 50ms, and pipeline latency acceptance under 100ms per NSe-SA1/PI1 specs.

nodes.name: TestPresetProperties
nodes.summary: Property tests verifying bandpass filter presets accept any configuration where low < high and reject equal low/high frequencies.

nodes.name: TestSignalQualityProperties
nodes.summary: Property test verifying that high SNR (>21dB) combined with low noise floor (<4.9uV RMS) is consistently classified as 'good' signal quality.

nodes.name: design_contracts.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic v2 domain contracts for NeuroSim visual network designer covering canvas component blocks, connections, graph validation, simulation preview limits, parameter sweeps, and multi-format export.

nodes.name: ComponentBlockContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for canvas component blocks with category literals (Neurons, Synapses, Encoders, Patterns) and optional neuron parameters with positive-count validation.

nodes.name: ConnectionContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for visual connections between populations with weight, synapse type, and a model validator preventing self-connections.

nodes.name: CanvasGraphContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for the complete canvas graph enforcing at least one node and validating that all edge source/target IDs reference existing nodes.

nodes.name: PreviewContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for simulation preview enforcing NS-S1 limits: max 500ms simulated duration and max 2000ms wall time.

nodes.name: ParameterSweepContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for parameter sweep mode enforcing 1-20 steps (NS-S2 limit) and ensuring sweep start < stop via model validator.

nodes.name: ExportFormatContract
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for multi-format export supporting cnl, nengo_python, c_header, neuroml, and svg formats with non-empty content validation.

nodes.name: verify-contracts-local.sh

nodes.name: verify_module

nodes.name: audit_workflows.py

nodes.name: topo_sort_issues

nodes.name: run_contract_ci.py

nodes.name: run_command
nodes.summary: Executes a shell command via subprocess in a given working directory, wrapping output in GitHub Actions group markers for collapsible log sections.

nodes.name: main

nodes.name: generate_tasks.py
nodes.summary: Generates markdown task files for all submodules (Neurosim, Neurobench, Neurochip, Neurosense, Neurohub, nmtk) by writing structured issue templates from a large in-memory task dictionary covering 70+ tasks.

nodes.name: ModuleStatus

nodes.name: ModuleProvider

nodes.name: MainScreen

nodes.name: CatalogScreen

nodes.name: DashboardScreen

nodes.name: goRouter
nodes.summary: Top-level GoRouter configuration declaring routes for dashboard (/), catalog (/catalog), and tool workspace (/tool/:moduleId) inside a ShellRoute.

nodes.name: python_setup.dart
nodes.summary: Flutter screen that guides users through installing Python 3.10+ when no interpreter is detected. Provides macOS Homebrew install, python.org download link, and a retry-detection button with live output display.

nodes.name: PythonSetupScreen
nodes.summary: StatefulWidget entry point for the Python setup screen. Delegates all state and UI to _PythonSetupScreenState.

nodes.name: _PythonSetupScreenState
nodes.summary: State class managing Python installation flow: runs 'brew install python' with live stdout streaming, opens python.org via url_launcher, and retries detection through ModuleProvider.recheckPython().

nodes.name: _installWithHomebrew
nodes.summary: Spawns 'brew install python' as a child process, streams stdout/stderr to a UI buffer, and triggers a recheck on success. Validates Homebrew availability first.

nodes.name: _retryCheck
nodes.summary: Triggers ModuleProvider.recheckPython() to re-probe for a working Python interpreter after user installation.

nodes.name: tool_view.dart
nodes.summary: Module workspace screen that embeds running module UIs via WebView with tab-based navigation. Polls each module's /health endpoint and falls back to system browser on unsupported platforms.

nodes.name: ToolViewScreen
nodes.summary: StatefulWidget accepting an initialModuleId to display a module's web UI. Delegates lifecycle and WebView management to _ToolViewScreenState.

nodes.name: _ToolViewScreenState
nodes.summary: Manages a map of WebViewControllers keyed by module ID, polls /health every 2 seconds per module, and renders an IndexedStack of WebViews with a ModuleTabBar for switching. Handles tab close, module stop, and browser fallback.

nodes.name: _pollModuleHealth
nodes.summary: Sets up a periodic timer (every 2s) that HTTP GETs the module's /health endpoint and marks it ready on 200, cancelling the timer once healthy.

nodes.name: _getController
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and caches a WebViewController per module, loading the module's frontend URL or its /docs endpoint for API-only modules.

nodes.name: bundle_manager.dart
nodes.summary: Singleton service that resolves paths for dev vs. bundled (standalone .app/.exe) modes, detects and caches a working Python interpreter across bundled/system/login-shell/well-known paths, and extracts bundled modules to Application Support on first launch.

nodes.name: PythonNotFoundException
nodes.summary: Custom exception thrown when no working Python 3.10+ interpreter can be found on the system.

nodes.name: BundleManager
nodes.summary: Singleton managing dual-mode path resolution (dev repo root vs. bundled .app/installer), a four-tier Python discovery strategy (bundled, PATH, login shell, well-known paths), and first-launch module extraction with version tracking.

nodes.name: findPython
nodes.summary: Probes for a working Python interpreter through four tiers: bundled binary, simple PATH commands, login-shell resolution via 'which', and well-known absolute paths (Homebrew, Anaconda, pyenv). Caches the first successful result.

nodes.name: extractModules
nodes.summary: Copies bundled module directories from .app/Contents/Resources/modules to ~/Library/Application Support, writing a version marker file to track extraction state and reporting progress via callback.

nodes.name: _resolveViaLoginShell
nodes.summary: Resolves a command name to an absolute path by running 'which' inside the user's login shell (zsh/bash -lc), picking up PATH from dotfiles that Finder-launched apps miss.

nodes.name: process_manager.dart
nodes.summary: Core service managing the full lifecycle of Python module processes: venv creation with pip bootstrap fallback, uvicorn launch, health polling, process stop with SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation, and persistent state saving to JSON.

nodes.name: ProcessRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract interface for process spawning (start and run), enabling dependency injection for testing the ProcessManager without real subprocesses.

nodes.name: DefaultProcessRunner
nodes.summary: Default implementation of ProcessRunner that delegates directly to dart:io Process.start and Process.run with all standard parameters.

nodes.name: ProcessManager
nodes.summary: Singleton orchestrating Python module lifecycle: creates venvs with pip/ensurepip/get-pip fallbacks, launches uvicorn processes, streams stdout/stderr, polls /health every 5s, kills zombie port holders, and persists module installation state to disk.

nodes.name: installModule
nodes.summary: Creates a Python venv (with --without-pip + ensurepip/get-pip.py fallback chain), installs local sibling dependencies, then runs 'pip install .' for the module. Reports progress and persists installed status.

nodes.name: startModule
nodes.summary: Launches a module's uvicorn server after killing any zombie process on the target port, auto-installing if venv is missing, and streaming stdout/stderr to a broadcast controller.

nodes.name: stopModule
nodes.summary: Sends SIGTERM to a running module process with a 5-second timeout, escalating to SIGKILL if the process does not exit gracefully.

nodes.name: _checkHealth
nodes.summary: HTTP GETs /health on a module's port, mapping status codes (200=running, 503=degraded, 404=running-no-endpoint) and broadcasting status changes. Uses HttpClient on native, http package on web.

nodes.name: saveModuleState
nodes.summary: Persists a module's state as JSON to the application documents directory, merging into an existing module_states.json file.

nodes.name: module_tab_bar.dart
nodes.summary: Horizontal tab bar widget displaying active modules with select and close callbacks. Each tab shows a frontend/API icon, module name, and close button with active-tab highlighting.

nodes.name: ModuleTabBar
nodes.summary: Stateless widget rendering a horizontal scrollable tab strip for active modules using Consumer<ModuleProvider>. Highlights the active tab with a primary-colored bottom border and delegates selection/close to parent callbacks.

layers.name: Contract-Driven Development Pipeline
layers.description: Python contracts, property-based tests, and automation scripts for multi-agent CDD validation across neuromorphic sub-projects.

layers.description: Main Dart application logic including screens, routing, state management providers, services, and models for the NeuroMorphicToolKit desktop/mobile app.

layers.name: Shared UI Component Library
layers.description: Reusable theme definitions, data models, and widget components in nmtk_ui_core consumed by the main Flutter application.

layers.description: Native platform-specific runner code (iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, Android) that bootstraps the Flutter engine on each target OS.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The Flutter desktop app begins in main.dart, which bootstraps NeuroToolkitApp. This file wires up providers (state management) and the router, making it the single point of initialization for the entire toolkit. Understanding this entry point reveals how NMTK presents itself as one unified app rather than six disconnected tools.
tour.languageLesson: Dart uses a top-level main() function as the entry point. The runApp() call hands control to the Flutter framework's widget tree.

tour.title: Routing and Navigation Shell
tour.description: The router defines every screen the user can reach and wraps them in a MainScreen shell with persistent navigation. With the highest fan-out (12 edges) among Dart files, it imports every screen and acts as the architectural spine of the UI. This is where you see the full menu of NMTK capabilities laid out.
tour.languageLesson: GoRouter is a declarative routing package for Flutter. Routes are defined as data structures rather than imperative Navigator.push calls.

tour.title: Module Data Model
tour.description: The Module class and its ModuleStatus enum are the core domain objects, referenced by 7 other files. Every neuromorphic tool (NeuroCNL, Neurosim, etc.) is represented as a Module instance with metadata like name, path, and lifecycle status. This shared vocabulary unifies how the app talks about its sub-tools.
tour.languageLesson: Dart enums can carry methods and implement interfaces, making ModuleStatus richer than a plain integer enumeration.

tour.title: ModuleProvider: Central State Hub
tour.description: ModuleProvider is the most-depended-upon node in the entire graph (fan-in 11). It manages the list of available modules, their runtime status, and notifies the UI of changes. Every screen that displays module information reads from this single source of truth, following the provider/ChangeNotifier pattern.
tour.languageLesson: Flutter's ChangeNotifier + Provider pattern is a lightweight reactive state management approach. Calling notifyListeners() triggers widget rebuilds.

tour.title: Dashboard and Catalog Screens
tour.description: The Dashboard provides a high-level overview of installed modules and system health, while the Catalog lets users browse and install new modules. Together they form the two primary views a user interacts with. Both consume ModuleProvider and delegate heavy lifting to services, keeping the UI layer thin.

tour.title: Process Manager: Module Lifecycle
tour.description: ProcessManager handles installing, starting, stopping, and health-checking each neuromorphic module as a subprocess. It is the bridge between the Flutter UI and the Python-based module backends. With fan-in 7 and fan-out 7, it sits at the center of the runtime graph, orchestrating the actual compute work.
tour.languageLesson: The ProcessRunner abstraction allows injecting a mock in tests (see MockProcessRunner), demonstrating Dart's interface-based dependency injection.

tour.title: Bundle Manager and Python Setup
tour.description: BundleManager discovers the Python environment and extracts module bundles from the app's assets. The PythonSetupScreen guides users through installing Python if it is missing. Together they solve the cross-language bootstrap problem: a Dart/Flutter app that needs a working Python runtime to operate its neuromorphic backends.

tour.title: UI Core Package: Shared Design System
tour.description: The nmtk_ui_core package is a separate Dart library that exports reusable widgets, theme tokens, and data models. With fan-out 10, it supplies components to both the main app and its tests. This separation enforces visual consistency across all module screens and enables independent UI testing.
tour.languageLesson: Dart packages use a barrel file (nmtk_ui_core.dart) to re-export public APIs. Consumers import one file instead of reaching into internal paths.

tour.title: Visualization Widgets
tour.description: Specialized widgets like NmtkEnergyBarChart, NmtkSparklineChart, and NmtkQuantizationTable render neuromorphic data visualizations. These depend on domain models (EnergyReport, QuantizationReport) and are consumed by module screens to display simulation results, sensor readouts, and benchmark metrics.

tour.title: NeuroCNL Contracts: Plain-English to SNN
tour.description: The NeuroCNL module uses Contract-Driven Development with Python dataclasses defining pipeline_contracts, neuron_params, and hardware_export. These contracts specify the exact shape of data flowing through the NLP-to-spiking-neural-network pipeline. The __init__.py re-exports them, forming the module's public API surface.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses with validation serve as lightweight schema enforcement, similar to TypeScript interfaces but with runtime checking.

tour.title: Cross-Module Contracts: Neurosim, Neurosense, Neurochip
tour.description: Each neuromorphic module defines its own contract files following the same CDD pattern. Neurosim's design_contracts define circuit components, Neurosense's signal_contracts specify sensor encoding formats, and Neurochip's deployment_contracts govern hardware flashing. This uniform contract structure makes it possible to compose modules into end-to-end pipelines.

tour.title: Property-Based Testing for Contracts
tour.description: PBT files like test_physics_properties and test_encoding_properties use Hypothesis-style generators to verify that contracts hold under randomized inputs. test_physics_properties has the highest fan-out (12) of any file in the graph, importing contracts from multiple modules to cross-validate physical constraints. This is how NMTK catches edge cases that example-based tests miss.
tour.languageLesson: Property-based testing (PBT) defines invariants rather than specific examples. The framework generates hundreds of random inputs to find violations.

tour.title: CDD Validation and Issue Generation
tour.description: The CDD pipeline has two key scripts: cdd_validation.sh auto-detects contract violations, and generate_cdd_pbt_issues.py converts failures into GitHub issues with labels and priorities. This closes the feedback loop: when a contract or property test breaks, the pipeline automatically creates trackable work items.

tour.title: Contract Verification and CI Scripts
tour.description: verify-contracts-local.sh runs contract checks locally before pushing, while scripts like run_mypy.sh and demo_smoke_test.sh form the broader quality gate. The publish_github_issues.py script in the GPT pipeline automates issue creation with topological sorting of dependencies. Together these scripts form the CI backbone that enforces CDD discipline across all modules.

tour.title: Testing the Flutter App
tour.description: The Dart test suite covers every major layer: widget_test verifies the app boots, catalog_test and dashboard_test check screen rendering with mock providers, process_manager_test validates subprocess lifecycle with MockProcessRunner, and launcher_e2e_test exercises end-to-end flows. This test architecture mirrors the production dependency graph, giving confidence that changes in services propagate correctly through the UI.
